description: Jam, then spoof: the fix is lost, a counterfeit signal takes over and walks the position off with a time offset, then a replay delay follows.
trainer_note: Sequence for the debrief: (1) jamming, SNR falls and the fix is lost; (2) the jamming eases and the receiver re-acquires onto counterfeit signals, which show a uniform raised SNR, so a fix comes back that looks healthy; (3) the position drifts 1.6 km and UTC gains 20 s; (4) after the drag-off is released a replay delay makes the plotter lag the ship by 30 s. HDT and VBW never change.

events.description: Jamming: jamming: received C/N0 falls by up to 38 dB (per-satellite spread 6 dB); satellites drop out and the fix is lost when fewer than four remain usable from T+240 s for 240 s (onset ramp 45 s, recovery ramp 30 s)

Counterfeit takeover and drag-off: position drag-off: the reported position walks 1600 m away towards 149 deg true (90 deg relative to the course at onset, then held) while the receiver keeps a valid fix (false track peaks at 6.00 m/s and 0.0600 m/s^2); every tracked satellite shows 45 dB-Hz while it lasts from T+500 s for 700 s (onset ramp 400 s, recovery ramp 0 s)
Time offset: time spoof: reported UTC moves +20.0 s from true; position stays true; every tracked satellite shows 45 dB-Hz while it lasts from T+700 s for 500 s (onset ramp 100 s, recovery ramp 0 s)
Replay delay: replay delay (meaconing style): position and time lags the truth by 30.0 s; the genuine C/N0 pattern is kept from T+1300 s for 360 s (onset ramp 60 s, recovery ramp 60 s)

timeline.text: the receiver has no fix (2 usable satellites, four needed)
the receiver reports a fix again (12 satellites used)
